question.problem:
Consider the following polynomial division: $$ \begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,5x-8 \\ & x+3\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,5{x}^{2}+\phantom{0}7x+\phantom{0}8\,\,\,} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,{5{x}^{2}+15x}_{―} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-8x+8 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-{8x-24}_{―} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,32\end{aligned} $$ From the above, we conclude the following:
$5{x}^{2}+7x+8$ $=$ {{field-1}} $+\,\,$ {{field-2}}
$x+3$ $x+3$
question.worked_solution:
$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,5x-8 \\  & x+3\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,5{x}^{2}+\phantom{0}7x+\phantom{0}8\,\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{5{x}^{2}+15x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-8x+8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-{8x-24}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,32\end{aligned}
$$

From the given polynomial division, we deduce that dividing the polynomial $5{x}^{2}+7x+8$ by the linear binomial $x+3$ gives

- the quotient $5x-8,$ and

- the remainder $32.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}+7x+8}{x+3}=5x-8+\frac{32}{x+3}.
$$
